# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence:** `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (SHA256 `3dc470f5490ec15b4024c513e87c67e0b17caeae2a2ce3d83541be24ef407e61`), 15,512 packets, capture window 2026-02-28 23:55:06 UTC to 2026-03-01 04:16:35 UTC (~4h21m). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory — analysis is based on the pcap alone.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.2/24 LAN, host **10.2.28.88** | Conversation stats; sole non-DC/gateway host generating traffic |
| MAC | **00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad** | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88` resolves to this MAC; matches `eth.src` on all frames sourced from 10.2.28.88 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** (domain `EASYAS123`, AD domain `easyas123.tech`) | DHCP `dhcp.option.hostname` for MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad; corroborated by NBNS name registration frames from 10.2.28.88 |
| Logged-in user | **brolf** | Kerberos `CNameString` field in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic sourced from 10.2.28.88 |

The AD domain controller is 10.2.28.2 (EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech); the bulk of LDAP/DCE-RPC/Kerberos/SMB traffic is normal domain-joined workstation activity and is not itself evidence of compromise.

## Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client). **Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The C2 session uses the exact wire format of the NetSupport remote-control protocol:

- Client requests carry `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and POST to `/fakeurl.htm`
- Server responses carry `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`
- Traffic uses the protocol's own command verbs — `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encrypted blob>` — over plaintext HTTP on TCP/443 (not TLS despite the port), which is the well-documented NetSupport RAT C2 beacon pattern.

## Indicators of compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **45.131.214.85:443** | TCP conversation 10.2.28.88:51912 <-> 45.131.214.85:443; carries all `fakeurl.htm` HTTP traffic |
| Domain | **vadusa.xyz** | DNS query from 10.2.28.88 at t=44.77s/44.81s resolving to A record 45.131.214.85, immediately followed by the first C2 TCP SYN to that IP at t=44.89s |
| URL | **http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm** | 264 HTTP POST requests to this exact path over the capture, first at t=45.05s, continuing at ~60s intervals then widening to a steady ~1-hour beacon cadence through t=15682s (end of capture) |
| Protocol markers | `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` / `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)` | Follow-TCP-stream output, stream index 40 (and repeated across the beacon session) |

No transferred executable, dropped file name, or file hash was observed in this capture — the RAT session is already established at the start of the capture window (first C2 SYN at t=44.9s, well before the capture's first Kerberos/DNS traffic settles), and no HTTP object transfer of a binary appears in the traffic. This pcap does not contain the initial infection/delivery vector; all `--export-objects http` artifacts recovered are non-malicious (Microsoft/Adobe/NVIDIA update and telemetry responses).

## Benign context (ruled out, not IOCs)

- 23.64.147.24, 23.218.232.148, 150.171.x.x, 23.192.223.x, 20.42.x.x, 13.107.x.x, 52.x.x.x — Akamai/Microsoft/Office 365/Windows Update/OneDrive/Skype CDN and telemetry endpoints (confirmed via TLS SNI: `login.microsoftonline.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, etc.)
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `services.gfe.nvidia.com`, `armmf.adobe.com`, `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` — routine NCSI/driver/Adobe update checks and an incidental browsing hit; no association with the C2 flow
- SMB/NBNS/LDAP/Kerberos/DCE-RPC to 10.2.28.2 — normal AD domain-membership traffic for DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR

## Incident summary

Windows workstation DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user **brolf**, is running a **NetSupport RAT** implant. The implant beacons over HTTP (mislabeled on TCP/443) to **vadusa.xyz / 45.131.214.85**, POSTing `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` requests to `/fakeurl.htm` with encrypted payloads, consistent with an attacker maintaining remote-control/screen-capture access. The RAT session is already active at capture start and persists for the full ~4.3-hour capture window with 264 observed C2 exchanges; the infection vector and any dropped binary are not present in this capture.
